_readme: Known files over the 500-line convention (CLAUDE.md, 'Code organization: 500-line file convention'), as of 2026-08-12. checkFileLength.mjs fails only if a file NOT listed here crosses 500 lines, or a listed file grows past the line count recorded here. Splitting a file below 500 lines does not require touching this file (the script reports it as a housekeeping notice instead of failing) but delete the entry once it's split. Do not bump a recorded number to silence a GREW violation — split the file, or if truly justified, say why right here.
_note_src_game_Game_ts: 1348->1256->1029 (2026-08-12): three form-(2) composition extractions have now landed — controllers/ForgeActions.ts, controllers/ScreenFlow.ts, and controllers/GameLoop.ts (the fixed-step sim + interpolated render main loop: update/advanceSim/stepSim/advanceOnline/spawnBulletTrails/updateFx/updateCamera/updateHud/pollConfirm, plus the accumulator/predictor/prevFire state that was purely internal to those methods). All three take Game as a narrow GameLoopHost/etc. callback interface (this repo's established host-callback-interface pattern, RunOutcome.ts/EventReactor.ts) and never call back into Game beyond that interface. GameLoop.ts got 17 tests against a real createGameEngine (same convention as controllers/ally.test.ts) plus faked Pixi collaborators; verified live via window.__game headless driving that an actual offline run/tutorial run/pause-freeze/resume/quit sequence produces the right tick counts and phase transitions, zero console errors. What's LEFT in Game.ts is: start()'s screen-callback wiring (~120 lines - inherently belongs in the assembly shell, fragmenting it further would hide the full picture of what connects to what), the constructor, run lifecycle (beginRun/beginTutorialRun/beginArenaDemoRun/finalizeOnlineRun/quitRun/resetRunRenderState - genuinely reads/writes phase/engine/session/meta/scene/roomBuilder in combination, see the same cross-call analysis from the two prior extractions), matchmaking/network glue, and thin host-interface implementations. Recorded as tracked debt; the run-lifecycle boundary specifically is the next real candidate if this gets revisited, not the whole file. 1029->1033 (2026-08-12, same day): +4 lines wiring `hud.onSwapWeapon` (the new idle-weapon-slot HUD chip's tap callback) straight to `builder.requestSwap()`, one line beside the existing `hud.onPause` wiring one line above it — the exact 'screen-callback wiring... inherently belongs in the assembly shell' category already called out above, not new debt shape.
